styleBrief:
This deck demands the visual language of a premium climate magazine — think National Geographic meets Bloomberg Green. Every card should feel like turning pages through an urgent yet beautiful editorial feature about our planet's technological transformation. We're using filled geometric variants throughout because the subject matter requires clarity and substance; outline variants would feel too tentative for such consequential content.

Commit to deep forest green (#2D4A3E) and warm sand (#F4E6D1) as alternating background colors, with electric blue (#0EA5E9) as the single accent color for text highlights. Forest green grounds the environmental theme while sand provides breathing room; electric blue represents innovation and energy flowing through the content. Every card gets one of these backgrounds — forest for the atmospheric moments, sand for the data-driven content. The electric blue highlight targets the emotional core words: "inflection," "revolution," "opportunity," "future" — never the structural terms. Behind-image cards use forest green as the overlay background to create that deep, cinematic atmosphere essential to climate storytelling.

Image rhythm follows an editorial magazine pattern: title card with sweeping renewable energy landscape, then alternate between atmospheric behind-image cards (solar fields, wind farms, industrial beauty shots with golden hour lighting) and structured sand-background cards with solidBoxes layouts for the economic data. The storage revolution and scale arrival cards demand behind-image treatment — these are the emotional peaks that need photographic weight. Use solidBoxes exclusively for the convergence economics, remaining challenges, and capital flows data, with each box colored in tonal variations of the forest green palette. Card 4 becomes our mandatory breather — just "Opportunity." in DISPLAY text over a dramatic clean energy installation shot. Never use outline variants, never cluster more than two data cards together, and never let the urgency of climate action feel clinical or sterile.
